findings.description: Body sections (1-9) use section-local citation numbers that collide with the declared-canonical unified bibliography [1]-[31], while section 0 and parts of 4.5 use the unified numbers; the two schemes are mixed without point-of-use warning. E.g. Gobburu 1999 (human PK, unified [4]) is cited inline as [2] in 2.4/2.5/4.1 but unified [2] is Ankersen 1998; Johansen 1999 IGF-1 finding (unified [10]) cited as [3] but unified [3] is PubChem; Svensson 2000 BMC (unified [11]) cited as [2]; Beck 2014 (unified [15]) cited as [1]/[3]; PCAC Oct-2024 (unified [22]) cited [4]; FR Doc (unified [23]) cited [7]; WADA (unified [24]) cited [8]. Following an inline marker to the canonical bibliography resolves to the wrong source. Fix: renumber inline refs to the unified scheme or state at first use that body numbering is section-local and decoded only by the crosswalk table.

Section 4.5 mixes both numbering schemes inside a single sentence: the Phase 1 study cited [2] (section-local) and the Phase 2 RCT cited [15] (unified). Sharpest instance of the citation-numbering defect.

Section 8 (regulatory, highest-stakes) cites the PCAC rationale as [10] and net-status as [12]; against the canonical bibliography these resolve to animal papers (Johansen 1999 rat bone; glucocorticoid-bone 2001 rat), not regulatory sources. Same root cause as the major finding.

Could state once plainly that the unknown chronic-SC risk is directionally asymmetric (7-day IV placebo-comparable AE rate cannot transfer to chronic SC self-administration). Section 7.7 nearly does this; a one-line elevation would close the only residual balance soft spot. Optional, non-blocking.
